- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. ## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

## omnifocus
OmniFocus is a GTD task manager. Hierarchy: Folders > Projects > Tasks > Subtasks.

TASK STATES: Available, Blocked, Deferred (future defer date), Flagged, Overdue, Completed, Dropped. Planned Date is a scheduling signal only — no availability/overdue constraints.

PROJECT TYPES: "sequential" (tasks in order; first incomplete = available, rest blocked; position = dependencies), "parallel" (all available), "single_actions" (no completion goal, cannot auto-complete). The `next` field is true for the first available action in a sequential project/action group; in parallel projects, all incomplete tasks have `next: true`.

ACTION GROUPS: Task with subtasks. Parent shows `blocked: true` while subtasks are active — this is normal, not an error. Do not try to unblock it.

INHERITED STATUS: `completed`/`dropped` reflect the task's own state, not its container's. `effectivelyCompleted`/`effectivelyDropped` reflect the container's state — if true, the task's parent project or action group was completed/dropped. Task in completed project: `completed: false`, `effectivelyCompleted: true`, `available: false`. Use `available_only=True` for actionable tasks.

EFFECTIVE DATES: Dates returned by get_tasks are always effective (inherited). A task with no direct due date WILL show its project's due date in the dueDate field — this is correct behavior, not a bug. You cannot clear an inherited date at the task level. Write operations set the task's own date.

RECURRING TASKS: `completed=True` uses `mark complete`, which creates the next occurrence. This is guaranteed. WARNING: Dropping a recurring task (status='dropped') without clearing recurrence first (recurrence='') spawns the next occurrence. To stop a series: update_tasks([{"id": "...", "recurrence": "", "status": "dropped"}]).

TAGS: Represent work contexts. Tag statuses: Active (normal), On Hold (tasks excluded from Available perspective), Dropped (tag hidden from picker; does NOT affect task availability).

DEFER vs DUE: Defer = hidden until that date. Due = deadline.

This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan or design. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan before building, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- seo-optimizer: Optimize content for search engines with keyword analysis, readability scoring, meta descriptions, and competitor comparison. Use this when users want to improve SEO, optimize blog posts, or analyze content for search performance.
- systems-thinking: Analyze problems using a Systems Thinking approach. Use when users mention "systems thinking," "systemic," "feedback loops," "unintended consequences," "root cause," "interconnected," or request analysis of complex, multi-factor problems. Guides conversation through questions and observations rather than prescriptive solutions.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- add-backlinks: Add backlinks from related blog posts and glossary entries to a target post. Use when the user wants to improve internal linking by having other content link back to a specific article.
- blog-post: Create or revise a blog post for the Agile Pain Relief website. Use when the user wants to write a new blog post, revise/refresh an existing one, or update content. Guides through gathering information, content structure, internal linking, and post-publish steps.
- evergreen-posting: Compile Mark's selected social drafts into the batch JSON the posting pipeline consumes (LinkedIn / Mastodon / Bluesky), validating character limits and URL budgets, threading the link when it won't fit, and marking the source calendars so nothing is promoted twice. Blog/glossary/newsletter prose is authored and selected UPSTREAM as Markdown via the vault linkedin-style draft skill; this skill condenses the selected options to three platforms and writes the JSON, it does not re-draft that prose. Quiz posts are still drafted here from seeds. Use when Mark says "build the batch JSON", "compile the selected drafts", "schedule social media", or asks for the evergreen batch.
- glossary-entry: Create a new glossary term for the Agile Pain Relief website. Use when the user wants to add a new Agile/Scrum term definition, concept explanation, or methodology entry to the glossary.
- indexing-strategy: Use this skill when Mark asks to analyze, plan, or implement SEO topic clusters and internal linking for agilepainrelief.com. Covers two modes: (1) ANALYZE mode — audit existing content, identify pillar/cluster opportunities, find gaps and orphaned pages, and produce a prioritized action plan; (2) IMPLEMENT mode — generate specific internal linking instructions, write or revise blog posts and glossary entries to fit the cluster strategy, and produce per-page checklists. Also use when Mark asks what a blog post or glossary entry needs for SEO, or when he wants to check whether a draft meets the cluster linking requirements.
- newsletter: Draft and send a newsletter to the Newsletter Subscribers list via Cakemail, starting from plain markdown. Use when Mark wants to write, render, test, or dispatch a newsletter / email campaign, or turn a markdown file into a Cakemail draft campaign. Drives the email-automation CLI's send-newsletter command.
- social-media-adapt: Adapt LinkedIn posts to Mastodon and Bluesky formats with platform-specific character limits, thread formatting, and JSON structure. Use when Claude needs to convert LinkedIn content to other social platforms, create threaded posts, or adapt content for different character limits (see the shared conventions for current limits).
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

content.content:
`src/send-newsletter.ts` renders a newsletter markdown file into HTML,
wraps it in the same MJML shell
used by the automation templates, and creates a draft campaign on the
`Newsletter Subscribers` list via the Cakemail `POST /campaigns` API.

**The authoring + send workflow lives in the `/newsletter` skill**
(`.claude/skills/newsletter/SKILL.md`): markdown file format, frontmatter,
Obsidian callouts (`[!quote]` / `[!action]`), the required `courses.json`
block, the `--test-send` / `--send` flag flow, and the sender/compliance notes.
Use that skill to draft or send a newsletter. The command reference below is
retained for quick lookup.

```bash
npm run send-newsletter -- --content newsletters/<file>.md [--test-send <email>] [--send | --schedule <day>] [--allow-past-courses] [--keep-on-error]
```

Every run creates a **brand-new** campaign (`POST /campaigns`); there is no
idempotency. Re-running the command is therefore how the whole list gets
emailed twice. Before creating, the CLI queries `findCampaignsByName` and
**aborts** if a campaign of the same name (`{date} - {subject}`) already exists
in a committed state (scheduled / delivering / delivered). There is **no
`--force`**: delete the existing campaign in Cakemail, then re-run. Same-name
*drafts* don't block (they can't send); they're listed as a cleanup nudge.

Flags:
- `--test-send <email>` creates the draft, then sends a `POST
  /campaigns/{id}/send-test` copy (`type=merged`) to the given address. This is
  the way to preview a newsletter: review it in your inbox and the Cakemail UI.
  **Preview-only: cannot be combined with `--send` or `--schedule`** (dispatch
  in a separate run). Combining preview with dispatch is what previously caused
  a "thought it was just a test" double-send.
- `--send` schedules the draft for immediate delivery (`POST
  /campaigns/{id}/schedule` with no date). Prompts `yes/no` before firing.
- `--schedule <day>` schedules delivery for the next `Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri` at
  10:00 AM Eastern (`POST /campaigns/{id}/schedule` with a `date` UNIX
  timestamp). Resolves to the soonest future 10am ET on that weekday; the
  `America/New_York` zone keeps it correct across EST/EDT. No confirmation
  prompt (the flag is the intent). Mutually exclusive with `--send`.
- `--allow-past-courses` bypasses the stale-course date check (the CLI aborts
  if `newsletters/courses.json` is missing/empty or holds a past-dated course).
- `--keep-on-error` leaves the draft in Cakemail if test-send or schedule
  fails. Default `DELETE /campaigns/{id}` keeps the UI tidy, since a failed
  send usually means re-running after a content fix.

The campaign is sent from sender ID `SENDER_ID_MARK` (=
`mark@agilepainrelief.com`), not the `contact@` sender used for transactional
course emails. The payload sets `content.default_unsubscribe_link: true`, so
Cakemail appends its own unsubscribe link and mandated postal-address footer.

**Greeting is code-owned, not authored.** `send-newsletter.ts` prepends the
greeting (`GREETING` = `Hi [firstname],`) to the body itself; the markdown file
must not contain one. `[firstname]` is Cakemail's no-fallback merge tag (blank
when the contact has no first name). NEVER use an empty fallback `[firstname,]`
— it's malformed and Cakemail prints the tag literally (this mailed the whole
list a literal `Hi [firstname,],` on 2026-06-26). A no-word fallback is

- `--schedule <day>` schedules delivery for the next `Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri` at

  `America/New_York` zone keeps it correct across EST/EDT. No confirmation
  prompt (the flag is the intent). Mutually exclusive with `--send`.

  if `newsletters/courses.json` is missing/empty or holds a past-dated course).
- `--keep-on-error` leaves the draft in Cakemail if test-send or schedule
  fails. Default `DELETE /campaigns/{id}` keeps the UI tidy, since a failed
  send usually means re-running after a content fix.

The campaign is sent from sender ID `SENDER_ID_MARK` (=
`mark@agilepainrelief.com`), not the `contact@` sender used for transactional
course emails. The payload sets `content.default_unsubscribe_link: true`, so

## Official Documentation

The main developer docs live at help.corsizio.com under the Developer API section. The documentation covers six areas: Endpoint & Authentication, Get Account Details, Get Events List, Get Event Details, Get Attendees List, and Get Attendee Details.

## AuthenticationYou must enable the API integration from inside your Account Integration Settings, after which you can copy and store the API Secret Access Key to use on all API requests. This step is required. All API endpoints must use the root path with the https request protocol. This lets a developer securely connect and pull event and attendee data from the account.

## Events Endpoints

**Get Events List** — `GET https://api.corsizio.com/v1/events`This endpoint queries the list of events from the account using multiple query string parameter filters, along with the ability to include additional data not normally included by default. You can also expand certain data types from their ID value to their full data model representation during parsing of your request.

Requests use a Bearer token header (`Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_API_SECRET_KEY}`) and support pagination via `limit` and `page` parameters. The JSON response includes `type`, an `account` object (id, name, alias, timeZone, currency, siteUrl), a `paging` object (page, limit, count, more), and a `list` array. Event objects contain fields such as `id`, `name`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `registrationCloseDate`, `displayDate`, `timeZone`, `location`, `priceFrom`, `priceTo`, a `prices` array with price/label pairs, `currency`, `pageUrl`, and `formUrl`.

**Get Event Details** — `GET https://api.corsizio.com/v1/events/{eventId}`If you need the attendees list for the event, use the `include` parameter to request attendees and optionally payment information for each attendee. Only use this option if you truly need that information, and you must have given the right permissions to your API Key from within your account integration settings. Event detail responses can include richer pricing data such as `earlyPrice` and `earlyBefore` fields.

## Third-Party Integrations

- **Make.com** — offers modules to list attendees, list events with filter criteria, and make custom API calls using authorized credentials. It requires an active Corsizio account with API integration enabled and an API secret access key.
- **MindCloud Universal API** — exposes 5 published actions for Corsizio, using a MindCloud API Key as a Bearer token plus a `connectionId` that selects the connected Corsizio account.

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `limit` | Number | "Limit the results list. Number between 1 and 100. Defaults to `20`" |
| `page` | Number | Pagination control, defaults to 1 |
| `order` | String | Sort by startDate, endDate, or created (use `-` prefix for descending) |
| `status` | String | Filter by: any, published, draft, archived, or deleted |
| `date` | Date Range | Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` or ranges like `2017-06-01:2017-06-30` |
| `price` | Number Range | Format: `FROM:TO` (e.g., `50:200`) |
| `category` | String ID | Filter by category ID |
| `location` | String ID | Filter by location ID |
| `age` | String ID | Filter by age group ID |
| `gender` | String ID | Filter by gender ID |
| `level` | String ID | Filter by level ID |
| `search` | String | Search event name or exact event ID |
| `include` | String List | Add optional data: details, filters, stats, config |
| `expand` | String List | Populate IDs as full objects: filters, instructors, account |

- id, name, startDate, endDate, registrationCloseDate
- displayDate, timeZone, location
- priceFrom, priceTo, prices (array with price/earlyPrice/label)
- currency, pageUrl, formUrl, photoUrl, mapUrl
- summary, summaryHtml, account

## Filtering for Upcoming/Active Events

Use the `date` parameter with future dates and set `status` to `published`.

**Note:** Rate limits are not mentioned in the documentation provided.

lastPrompt: We have two places mention course dates: email-automation/courses and on each of the course pages.  Is there an elegant way to derive all of them from one place? Even better would if we pull them from…

content.text:
Yes — and there's a stronger case for it than you probably realised, because it's **four** places, not two, and three of them are currently stale.

## What I found

| Place | What it holds | Current state |
|---|---|---|
| `src/content/courses/*/index.mdx` → `workshops.workshops[]` | free-text `date`, `location`, Corsizio event URL | CSPO still lists **June 11-12, 2026**; CSD-technical still lists **June 22-25, 2026**. Both past. |
| `email-automation/newsletters/courses.json` | `date`, `dateFormatted`, `location`, Corsizio URL | Lists **July 28-29** CSM (past); lists the Aug 11-14 CSPO the CSM page doesn't. |
| `email-automation/courses/{csm,cspo,csd}-virtual.json` | cohort `date`, `numberOfDays`, `duration` + Zoom/Mural/Dropbox | `csm-virtual.json` says **2026-06-15** — two cohorts behind. |
| `src/content/pages/surviving-the-ai-tsunami…/index.mdx` | `eventId` + six hand-written `scheduleDetails` bullets | Separate shape; not really the same problem. |

And a fifth consumer downstream: `src/components/courses/structured-data.astro:27` regex-parses those free-text date strings to decide which events go into JSON-LD, with `!workshopDate → include`. So a date it can't parse gets emitted to Google as a live event forever. Course prices are also hardcoded there (`:60-77`) while Corsizio holds the real ones.

## Corsizio can be the source — for two of the four

`GET https://api.corsizio.com/v1/events`, bearer token from Account → Integration Settings. Event objects carry `id`, `name`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `displayDate`, `timeZone`, `location`, `priceFrom`/`priceTo`/`prices[]`, `currency`, `pageUrl`, `formUrl`, `registrationCloseDate`. Filters: `status=published`, `date=2026-08-04:`, `order=startDate`, `category`. That covers everything the site listings and the newsletter block need, including the prices in the JSON-LD.

It **cannot** be the source for `email-automation/courses/*.json`, and shouldn't try: Zoom URL, Mural board, Google Docs folder, workbook URL are per-cohort things Corsizio has never heard of. What it *can* do there is kill the hand-typed `date` / `numberOfDays` / `duration` — replace them with a single `corsizioEventId`, and let `course-config.ts` resolve start/end from the API. That file stops being "a date I retyped" and becomes "a pointer plus the four links only I have."

## The design I'd recommend

One generated file, `shared/course-schedule.json`, written by `npm run sync-courses` (a peer of the existing `posthog-export.ts` — same pattern: script hits an API, writes a checked-in artefact). Keyed by course code, an array of `{eventId, startDate, endDate, displayDate, location, pageUrl, price}`, past events filtered at generation time.

Then: the Astro course pages read it via a small `src/lib/courses.ts` keyed off a new `courseCode` frontmatter field (frontmatter keeps `heading`/`body`, loses the array); `structured-data.astro` gets real ISO dates and real prices and the regex block dies; `send-newsletter.ts` reads it instead of `newsletters/courses.json`; `course-config.ts` resolves its dates through `eventId`.

**Commit the generated file rather than fetching at build.** It's in `shared/`, so writing it triggers a Netlify rebuild on push, which is exactly the behaviour you want. A build-time fetch would mean a Corsizio outage takes your deploy down, and you'd still need scheduled builds to pick up a new event — so you get the fragility without escaping the staleness. Committed, you get deterministic builds, a git history of schedule changes, and the option to add a nightly job later that runs the sync and pushes if the diff is non-empty.

The one real design decision is **mapping Corsizio events to course slugs**. Cleanest is Corsizio categories (`expand=filters` gives you category objects) with an explicit `categoryId → slug` table in one constants file; matching on `name` regex works today but breaks the first time you rename an event. Worth checking what categories you actually have set up before committing to it.

## Cost

Roughly half a day: sync script + schema/frontmatter change + rewriting `structured-data.astro` + repointing the newsletter and course-config readers. The `surviving-the-ai-tsunami` page I'd leave alone — its schedule is prose about daylight-saving shifts, not a listing.

Two things I'd want from you before building: whether you have Corsizio categories set per course (or want to map by event-id list), and whether killing `newsletters/courses.json` is fine or the newsletter needs to hand-pick which upcoming courses appear.

Sources: [Endpoint & Authentication](https://help.corsizio.com/article/37-api-endpoint-authentication), [Get Events List](https://help.corsizio.com/article/39-api-get-events-list), [Get Event Details](https://help.corsizio.com/article/41-api-get-event-details)

content.text:
Yes — 2.5 is right, and the cohort config is the correct half. Concretely:

```jsonc
{
  "type": "CSM",
  "corsizioEventId": "6a468a876879da6e4b6bfca0",  // replaces date + numberOfDays
  "duration": "08:59-17:01",                       // stays local — see below
  "muralLink": "...", "googleDocsFolder": "...", "dropboxFolder": "...",
  "meetingInvite": { "zoomUrl": "...", "invitationUrl": "..." }
}
```

Everything that's left is genuinely yours and nowhere else. The payoff isn't the typing saved, it's that `eventId` becomes a **join key**: the course page's workshop button and the cohort config now provably point at the same cohort, so `csm-virtual.json` saying June 15 while the site sells September 3 stops being representable.

Three things that change the design though:

**The email path can't read the generated file.** `shared/course-schedule.json` is filtered to future events, but the post-course email goes out *after* the class. So `course-config.ts` needs `GET /v1/events/{eventId}` — a by-id lookup, no date filter. That's fine (it's a CLI already making network calls), but the docs are silent on whether by-id resolves *past* events. If it doesn't, the fix is to have the send cache the resolved dates back into the cohort file on first read, so the post email works off what the pre-7day email already fetched. Worth testing against a finished cohort before building.

So: site reads a committed artefact, email-automation does a live by-id lookup. Two mechanisms, but they're answering different questions ("what's on sale" vs "what was this cohort"), so that's correct rather than inconsistent.

**Keep `duration` local.** `startDate`/`endDate` are full ISO datetimes, so Corsizio would hand back 09:00-17:00 — but your default is `08:59-17:01`, which is a deliberate padding fudge for the calendar invites, not the advertised time. Deriving it would silently rewrite every Google/Outlook invite. Make it an optional override that defaults to the current constant, unset for most cohorts.

**`numberOfDays` is derivable only for consecutive days.** `endDate - startDate + 1` is right for CSM/CSPO/CSD; it would be nonsense for anything on the tsunami cadence. Fine to derive with that assumption stated, since the three certification courses are the only consumers.

One open question I can't settle from the docs: for a multi-day event like the Aug 11-14 CSPO, I don't know whether Corsizio stores `endDate` as the last day's end time (which gives you both fields free) or models the four mornings as a session list under one event. Five minutes with a real key against that event answers it, and it decides whether `numberOfDays` comes from the API or stays hand-set.

That needs you to enable the API in Account → Integration Settings and drop the key in the root `.env`.

content.text:
All three questions answered, plus two things I wasn't looking for. (`temp/` is gitignored, so the raw dumps and the probe stay out of the repo.)

## Q1: multi-day — comes free, and so does `duration`

One event, not a session list (`breakdownDates: []` on every course). `startDate`/`endDate` are full ISO UTC datetimes spanning first-day-start → last-day-end:

| Event | startDate / endDate | displayDate |
|---|---|---|
| CSPO Aug 11-14 | `2026-08-11T13:00Z` → `2026-08-14T17:00Z` | Tue, Aug 11, 9:00 AM EDT – Fri, Aug 14, 1:00 PM EDT |
| CSD Jun 22-25 | `2026-06-22T16:30Z` → `2026-06-25T21:00Z` | Mon, Jun 22, 12:30 PM EDT – Thu, Jun 25, 5:00 PM EDT |
| CSM Sep 3-4 | `2026-09-03T13:00Z` → `2026-09-04T21:00Z` | Thu, Sep 3, 9:00 AM EDT – Fri, Sep 4, 5:00 PM EDT |

So `numberOfDays` is a day span, and `duration` falls out of the times: CSD gives **12:30-17:00**, which is exactly the hand-typed value in `csd-virtual.json`. CSPO gives 9:00-13:00, matching "4 mornings, 9am-1pm ET". Only CSM differs, and only because `08:59-17:01` is your deliberate calendar padding against Corsizio's 9:00-17:00. So: derive both, keep `duration` as an optional local override for the padding, and the cohort config shrinks to `corsizioEventId` + the four links.

One implementation note: the datetimes are UTC with `timeZone: "America/Toronto"` as a separate field. Day span has to be computed **in that zone**, not from raw UTC milliseconds, or an early/late event rounds to the wrong number of days.

## Q2: past-by-id — works

All three past events returned HTTP 200 with full data. `course-config.ts` can resolve dates by id at post-course-email time, no local cache, no archive file. The only 404 is a *deleted* event — which brings me to the thing I wasn't looking for.

## Q3: mapping — solved, one wrinkle

All 53 events carry exactly one category, ids stable:

```
67e30b6100cd6ddccedcc2c1  n=15  Certified ScrumMaster training
67e4270400cd6ddccefef17c  n=14  Certified Scrum Product Owner training
67e4271d00cd6ddccefef4db  n=13  Advanced Certified ScrumMaster training
67fd4bae00cd6ddcceb14a06  n= 8  Certified Scrum Professional – ScrumMaster training
69cd8eb84fa9204f41054cc2  n= 1  Certified Scrum Developer Training
68f253e18289735f6334a11e  n= 1  Scrum Better with Kanban
6a106e4c8bc748bdca8e91bc  n= 1  Agile and GenAI
```

Zero uncategorised, zero multi-category. `categoryId → slug` table, no name matching.

The wrinkle: you have **one** CSD category but **two** CSD course pages (technical and nontechnical). Cleanest fix is a second Corsizio category — a one-time click in your account, and the mapping stays a pure table. The alternative is a name-contains-`(Technical)` special case, which is the thing I'd rather not build.

## Two things I wasn't looking for

**A dead registration link.** `newsletters/courses.json` lists CSM July 28-29 at event `6a2317055fe95b0ca46f4539`. That id 404s, and a `search` across `status=any|archived|draft|deleted` returns count 0 — it doesn't exist in any state. If a newsletter shipped that entry, subscribers got a broken register link.

**A wrong price in your JSON-LD.** `structured-data.astro:74` hardcodes CSD at **1195**; Corsizio says 995 (personal) / 1095 (regular). That's being published to Google as structured data. Deriving prices from `prices[]` fixes it and picks up `earlyPrice`/`earlyBefore` (the Tsunami course has 1099 with 949 before Sept 8) for free.

And the live truth is only **three** future events — CSPO Aug 11-14, CSM Sep 3-4, Tsunami Sep 28. Your CSPO and CSD-technical pages are currently advertising June classes that have already run.

102	    );
103

input.command:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import pathlib, re
p = pathlib.Path('scripts/corsizio-sync.ts')
t = p.read_text()

# 1. import the shared client
t = t.replace(
"""import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'url';
""",
"""import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'url';
import {
  type CorsizioEvent,
  countDays,
  fetchPublishedEvents,
  partsIn,
} from '../shared/corsizio';
""", 1)

# 2. drop the now-shared API constant
t = t.replace("const API = 'https://api.corsizio.com/v1';\n", "", 1)

# 3. drop the locally-declared Corsizio types (now imported)
t = re.sub(
    r"// --- Corsizio types \(only the fields we consume\) -+\n\n.*?\n\ninterface EventsListResponse \{\n.*?\n\}\n\n",
    "", t, count=1, flags=re.DOTALL)

# 4. drop the local partsIn / countDays (now shared)
t = re.sub(r"/\*\* Calendar parts \(y/m/d/h/min\) of an instant, as seen in `timeZone`\. \*/\nfunction partsIn.*?\n\}\n\n",
           "", t, count=1, flags=re.DOTALL)
t = re.sub(r"/\*\* Calendar days spanned, inclusive, counted in the event's timezone\. \*/\nfunction countDays.*?\n\}\n\n",
           "", t, count=1, flags=re.DOTALL)

# 5. drop the local fetchAllEvents
t = re.sub(r"async function fetchAllEvents.*?\n\}\n\n", "", t, count=1, flags=re.DOTALL)
t = t.replace("const events = await fetchAllEvents(loadKey());",
              "const events = await fetchPublishedEvents(loadKey());", 1)

p.write_text(t)
print("rewrote scripts/corsizio-sync.ts")
PYEOF

input.command:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import json, pathlib, collections

# Cohort -> Corsizio event id. These are the events each config currently
# describes; CSM's config was two cohorts stale, so it moves to the live one.
ids = {
    'csm-virtual.json':  ('6a468a876879da6e4b6bfca0', True),   # Sept 3-4 (was stale at 2026-06-15)
    'cspo-virtual.json': ('6a23328e5fe95b0ca47759ce', False),  # Aug 11-14
    'csd-virtual.json':  ('69cd8ce7066b8e5ce999e15d', False),  # June 22-25
}

for name, (event_id, keep_padding) in ids.items():
    p = pathlib.Path('email-automation/courses') / name
    cfg = json.loads(p.read_text(), object_pairs_hook=collections.OrderedDict)
    out = collections.OrderedDict()
    out['type'] = cfg['type']
    out['corsizioEventId'] = event_id
    # CSM alone keeps an explicit window: 08:59-17:01 deliberately brackets the
    # 9-to-5 class by a minute either side in the calendar invite. CSD's old
    # hand-typed 12:30-17:00 exactly matches Corsizio, so it can go.
    if keep_padding:
        out['duration'] = '08:59-17:01'
    for k, v in cfg.items():
        if k in ('type', 'date', 'numberOfDays', 'duration'):
            continue
        out[k] = v
    p.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(f'{name}: {cfg.get("date")} -> event {event_id}')
PYEOF

diff --git a/HISTORY.md b/HISTORY.md
index 1c5028ab..a90201f7 100644
--- a/HISTORY.md
+++ b/HISTORY.md
@@ -6,0 +7,61 @@ Newest first. (Detailed, current behaviour lives in `CLAUDE.md`; this file is th
+## 2026-08-04 — Quiz results: a shape instead of a balance bar, and the move stops going silent
+
+**Why.** The `map-move` results page led with a two-segment balance bar: the
+proportion of gaining to slipping answers. It could say "this much of your time
+was well spent" and nothing else, so it could not answer the question the page
+exists to answer, which is why one area deserves attention ahead of another.
+
+A radar chart was the first idea and was wrong, for a reason worth writing down:
+**a radar needs a number on every axis, and this quiz deliberately has none.**
+Answers are classified, not scored. Drawing one would have meant inventing the
+numbers and then presenting them as measurement, and a `context` answer ("there
+is no Product Owner I can coach") would have plotted as a low point, reading as
+the taker's failing when the whole design says it is not.
+
+**What replaced it.** A fixed grid of named kinds of work, each carrying a bar
+showing how much of the taker's time went to it. Two new per-option fields feed
+it, `box` and `weight`, both independent of `bucket`: the bucket says
+strength-or-gap, the box says what kind of work, and those are genuinely
+orthogonal ("almost no time on coaching" is a slipping answer about an
+appreciating box). There is still no number on the page.
+
+**The mosaic that lost, and why it matters.** The first build drew each box at
+the actual size of its share, which is a better picture of where the time went
+and was the version everyone preferred on sight. It failed on the case the page
+exists for. The box being recommended is by definition the one the taker has
+given least time to, so it was always the smallest box on the picture and always
+the first too small to hold its own label. Label thresholds, a fallback key
+below the picture, and finally the move tag migrating into that key were all
+machinery to paper over a picture arguing against its own recommendation. Fixed
+boxes plus a bar say the same thing about proportion and guarantee every box can
+be read. Worth knowing before anyone rebuilds the mosaic.
+
+**Three more things fell out of building it, each worth keeping.**
+
+_A quadrant needed a fourth box that could not exist._ Splitting the bottom row
+by scope (one person versus wider than the team) produced "your own overhead",
+which exactly one option in thirty-two could reach, and only if the taker was
+part-time. For a full-timer the box was not rare, it was unreachable. Adding a
+ninth question to fill it made things worse, not better: it converted an empty
+box into an unlabellable sliver and pushed label eviction from 17% to 34%. The
+fix was to stop splitting the row. Every automatable thing a Scrum Master does is
+mechanical, whether it is a ticket, a status round-up or a set of slides.
+
+_The arrow had to go._ A curve from the box to take time from to the box to put
+it into was hard to follow and made the picture busy. Two accent words on the two
+boxes say the same thing and nothing crosses the picture.
+
+**The bug this uncovered.** `eligible()` in `map-move.ts` accepted any `slipping`
+answer for a half of the move whether or not a sentence existed for that half.
+`q2`'s "status and logistics desk" sits first in `redirectPriority` and has a
+`reclaimSentence` but no `redirectSentence`, so on **16% of all answer sets** it
+won the redirect and then rendered nothing: the taker was told what to stop doing
+and never told where the time should go. Worse, once the shape existed it also
+put "more of this" on the mechanical work, which is advice to spend more time on
+the coordination machine. Requiring the sentence (already the rule for `context`
+answers) makes the walk carry on to the next candidate that has something to say.
+
+Measured over all 65,536 answer sets, complete moves went from 52.0% to 65.9%,
+and a new `reclaimSentence` on `q1`'s part-time answer took it to 74.7%. Nothing
+ever renders empty, before or after.
+

Course pages are driven by frontmatter (schema in `src/content.config.ts`) for everything **except the schedule**. Workshop dates, times and prices come from Corsizio — see "Course schedule (Corsizio)" below. Frontmatter's `workshops` block holds only the copy that wraps them:

```yaml
workshops: { heading: 'Upcoming Workshops', body: '...' }
```

### Course schedule (Corsizio)

**Corsizio is the source of truth for when a public course runs and what it costs.** Nothing in this repo hand-maintains a course date. `npm run sync-courses` (`scripts/corsizio-sync.ts`) pulls published events from the Corsizio API and writes **`shared/course-schedule.json`**; everything downstream reads that generated file.

Run it whenever you schedule, move, or cancel a course in Corsizio, then commit the result. `--dry-run` prints what would change without writing.

- **The generated file is committed on purpose.** It sits in `shared/`, so pushing it triggers a Netlify rebuild, and a Corsizio outage can never break a deploy. It also gives a git history of schedule changes. A build-time fetch would buy fragility without escaping staleness (you would still need scheduled builds to notice a new event).
- **Consumers.** Site: `src/lib/courses.ts` (`workshopsFor(slug)`) feeds the course pages, the "Get Certified" tabs, and the JSON-LD in `src/components/courses/structured-data.astro`. Email: `email-automation/src/send-newsletter.ts` builds the Upcoming Courses block from the same file. The `email-automation/courses/*.json` cohort configs instead resolve **by event id, live** — see below.
- **Mapping is by Corsizio category, not event name.** `CATEGORY_TO_COURSE` in the sync script maps each category id to a `src/content/courses/` slug. Every event carries exactly one category and the ids are stable, so retitling a workshop can't break the mapping. A category with no row is reported loudly by the sync and its events are invisible on the site until someone adds one. `slug: null` means "a real course that deliberately isn't a course-collection page" (the AI Tsunami, which is a marketing page). Only the **Technical** CSD track is scheduled, so the single CSD category maps to the Technical page and the Nontechnical page always shows the placeholder.
- **Dates are UTC instants plus a separate `timeZone`.** Every label and day count is computed in the event's own zone (`shared/corsizio.ts`), never from raw UTC milliseconds, or a 9am Toronto class can round onto the wrong calendar day. `startDate` is the first day's start and `endDate` the last day's end, which is what makes `numberOfDays` and the daily time window derivable. That holds because none of our courses use Corsizio's `breakdownDates` (per-session hours); one that did would need different handling.
- **Only future events are written.** A course that has already run drops out of the file at the next sync, which is the drift this replaced: course pages were advertising classes that had already happened, and a cancelled course kept a dead "Register" link in the newsletter.

**Cohort configs resolve live, not from the file.** `email-automation/courses/{csm,cspo,csd}-virtual.json` hold a `corsizioEventId` plus only what Corsizio has never heard of (Zoom, Mural, docs folders). `resolveCourseConfig()` in `course-config.ts` fetches the event by id and fills in `date` / `numberOfDays` / `duration` before anything renders. It uses a **live by-id lookup rather than the generated file** because the post-course email is sent *after* the class, when the event is no longer in the future-filtered schedule. A by-id lookup works fine for past events; a *deleted* one 404s, and that throws rather than falling back to a stale date, so a cancelled course is caught before anyone is emailed. `duration` stays overridable per cohort: CSM sets `"08:59-17:01"` so the calendar invite brackets the 9-to-5 class by a minute either side. Delete that line to adopt Corsizio's exact times.

## Global Page Blocks (Layout-Level)

1	# Agile Pain Relief Astro - Project Documentation
2	
3	## Project Overview
4	
5	Astro-based website for Agile Pain Relief Consulting with blog posts, glossary terms, courses, and pages.
6	
7	**Tech Stack:** Astro 7, React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, MDX, TypeScript, Pagefind, Netlify
8	
9	**Build Commands:**
10	
11	- `npm run dev` - Development server with drafts enabled
12	- `npm run build` - Production build with Pagefind indexing
13	- `npm run preview` - Preview production build
14	
15	**This repo is the only source of truth for the website.** Specs, handoff docs and design briefs in Mark's Obsidian vault (or anywhere else outside the repo) are transitional working material: they get deleted, and they go stale the moment the code moves on. Never cite an external path as the authority for how something works, and never send a future reader there to find out. When such a doc informs a decision, copy the part that still matters into `CLAUDE.md`, `HISTORY.md`, an ADR, or a code comment, and drop the pointer. The exceptions are genuinely external, genuinely durable sources: vendor documentation, and the read-only material in `reference/`.
16	
17	**Change log:** `HISTORY.md` (repo root) is the plain-English "why we did it" log, newest first. After any notable change or architectural decision, add a short dated entry there. This `CLAUDE.md` documents how things work _now_; `HISTORY.md` records why they got that way. `NOTES.md` (repo root) is a terse authoring cheat-sheet (component snippets, MD-vs-MDX, gotchas) for hands-on content work.
18	
19	## Top-level directories
20	
21	- `src/` — Astro site (pages, components, content)
22	- `shared/` — Code and data used by both the Astro site and the email-automation CLI: `cakemail-constants.ts` (list/sender IDs, From name/address, form URLs), `corsizio.ts` (the Corsizio API client, used by the schedule sync and the course-email CLI but never by the site itself), and the generated `course-schedule.json`. Changes here DO trigger Netlify rebuilds.
23	- `email-automation/` — Node.js CLI for sending course emails via Cakemail. Has its own `package.json` / `tsconfig.json` / `.env`. Run commands from inside `email-automation/`. See `email-automation/CLAUDE.md` for details. Changes to this directory do NOT trigger Netlify rebuilds (see `netlify.toml`).
24	- `pandoc/` — Brand-styled Typst template and build script for turning vault markdown into lead-magnet PDFs. See "Lead-magnet PDFs" below.
25	- `docs/adr/` — Architecture Decision Records, for choices where the rejected options matter as much as the chosen one (currently: the unguessable-slug workbook gate). `CLAUDE.md` says how a thing works; an ADR says what else was considered and why it lost. Add one only when that trade-off is worth preserving.
26	- `reference/` — Read-only source material consulted while writing site content (e.g. point-in-time captures of Scrum Alliance course pages). Not code, not published, never imported by the build. See `reference/README.md`.
27	- `scripts/` — Repo-level utility scripts run through npm (currently `posthog-export.ts`).
28	- `bombadil/` — Browser-test specs run by `npm run test:browser`; results land in `.bombadil-out/`.
29	- `temp/` — Scratch space for one-off previews and downloads. Not built, not shipped.
30	
31	### Post-course newsletter signup (prefilled Cakemail form)
32	
33	Post-course emails sent by `email-automation/` include a "Subscribe to the Newsletter" link pointing at `/newsletter-subscribe/` (`src/pages/newsletter-subscribe.astro`) with the student's details prefilled in the query string: `?email=…&custom_attributes[firstname]=…&auto_submit=1`. That page embeds a Cakemail form bound to the Newsletter Subscribers list (double opt-in); Cakemail's `form-prefill.js` reads the params off the page URL, fills the form, and auto-submits it. The link is built by `buildPrefillSignupUrl()` in `email-automation/src/signup-url.ts`.
34	
35	There is **no server-side endpoint, HMAC signature, or OAuth token** in this path (it predates and is separate from the Turnstile gate below). Double opt-in is the abuse guard: a forged link can only send a confirmation email to the address that owns it, which never subscribes without the click. This prefilled-link path stays fully client-side; the general newsletter form, the AI forms, and the quiz instead route through the Turnstile-gated `/api/newsletter-signup` endpoint (see "Signup bot protection" below).
36	
37	The Newsletter Subscribers list ID is not a secret and lives in `shared/cakemail-constants.ts` as `NEWSLETTER_SUBSCRIBERS_LIST_ID`.
38	
39	### Signup bot protection: Turnstile gate (`/api/newsletter-signup`)
40	
41	All browser signups except the post-course prefilled link (the general newsletter form, both AI lead-magnet forms, and the quiz capture) POST same-origin to `/api/newsletter-signup` (`src/pages/api/newsletter-signup.ts`, `prerender = false` so it deploys as a Netlify function). The function verifies a **Cloudflare Turnstile** token and only then forwards the multipart submission to one consolidated Cakemail hosted form, server-side. This replaced the old browser-direct POSTs, which exposed the raw Cakemail form URL in the client bundle where bots scraped it and submitted junk (a client-side honeypot never sees a direct POST).
42	
43	- **Turnstile keys are static (no rotation).** Public site key: a constant in `src/constants/turnstile.ts` (baked into the client bundle — a `PUBLIC_` env var would offer no advantage). Secret: Netlify env `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`, read at runtime via `process.env` so a key change needs no redeploy. **No Cakemail credentials** are involved — the hosted form accepts anonymous POSTs, so the function only verifies + forwards (this is why it's set-and-forget, unlike the old OAuth path).
44	- **The Cakemail form URL is server-only:** `src/lib/server/cakemail-forms.ts` (`CAKEMAIL_FORM_URL` + `cakemailFormUrlFor()`), removed from `shared/cakemail-constants.ts` so it never reaches the browser. One consolidated form serves every purpose; the client sends a `form` field (`newsletter` | `ai` | `quiz`) that currently all map to the one URL but leave room to split a purpose back onto its own form.
45	- **Shared widget:** `src/components/global/turnstile.tsx` (`<Turnstile onToken onExpire ref>`; loads the script once per page, explicit render). Each form keeps a `token` + `submitError`, blocks submit until a token exists, appends `cf-turnstile-response` + `form`, and resets the widget on failure. The submission is now same-origin (not `no-cors`), so the form reads the real response.
46	
47	### Self-hosted quiz engine (`src/lib/quiz-engine/`)
48	
49	Quizzes are authored as MDX files in `src/content/quizzes/{slug}/index.mdx` and rendered by a small, self-contained engine in `src/lib/quiz-engine/`. The engine is designed to be extractable to a standalone open-source Astro package later, so it has no imports from APR-specific code. See `src/lib/quiz-engine/README.md` for the engine's public API and authoring guide.
50	
51	Routes (APR-specific, consume the engine):
52	
53	- `/quiz/{slug}/` — landing page (`src/pages/quiz/[slug].astro`). Renders hero + category cards + persuasion block from frontmatter, then mounts the React `QuizStepper` island.
54	- `/quiz/{slug}/results/` — results page (`src/pages/quiz/[slug]/results.astro`, SSR). Dispatches on the quiz's `resultStyle` frontmatter field (`'band'` | `'map-move'`, default `'band'`). **Band** reads `?total=&max=&level=&{sectionId}={level}` and renders the matching `<ResultCard>` blocks from the quiz's MDX body. **Map-move** reads the raw answers from a single `?a=` param and renders the `MapMoveResults.astro` engine component (a per-answer map + one recommended move) directly from frontmatter, not the MDX body. Both query strings are intentionally unsigned: anyone can craft a URL to view a tier/result. If tamper-resistance becomes important, sign the query in the browser before redirect and verify on the page.
55

## 2026-08-04 — Course dates come from Corsizio, not from four hand-typed copies

**Why.** Course dates lived in four places: the `workshops` array in each course
page's frontmatter, `email-automation/newsletters/courses.json` for the
newsletter, the `date` in each `email-automation/courses/*.json` cohort config,
and the AI Tsunami page's prose. Three of the four were wrong on the day this was
written. The CSPO and CSD-technical pages were still advertising June classes
that had already run. `csm-virtual.json` said June 15 while the site sold
September 3. And `newsletters/courses.json` listed a July 28 CSM whose Corsizio
event returned 404 in every status: the course was cancelled after the newsletter
went out, so subscribers were sent a dead "Register" link. Nothing was broken in
a way anything would report; four copies of a fact simply drift.

**What it is now.** Corsizio is the source of truth. `npm run sync-courses`
writes `shared/course-schedule.json`, and the course pages, the "Get Certified"
tabs, the JSON-LD and the newsletter all read it. The cohort configs keep only
what Corsizio has never heard of (Zoom, Mural, docs folders) plus a
`corsizioEventId`; their dates resolve live. So it is two and a half places
collapsed into one, the half being the cohort config, which had to keep its own
file because no calendar system knows our Mural board.

**Why the file is committed rather than fetched at build.** A build-time fetch
would let a Corsizio outage break a deploy, and would *still* need scheduled
builds to notice a newly-scheduled course, so it buys fragility without escaping
staleness. Committed in `shared/`, pushing it triggers the rebuild by itself and
git records every schedule change.

**Why the email path fetches live anyway.** The generated file holds only future
events, but the post-course email is sent *after* the class, when the cohort's
event is no longer in it. So `resolveCourseConfig()` does a by-id lookup, which
Corsizio answers for past events. Two mechanisms, because they answer different
questions: "what is on sale" versus "what was this cohort". A deleted event 404s
and throws rather than falling back to a stale local date, so the cancelled-course
case that produced the dead newsletter link now stops a send instead.

**Mapping is by category id, not event name.** Every Corsizio event carries
exactly one category and the ids are stable, so retitling a workshop cannot break
the mapping; matching on names would have. Two things fell out of the probe worth
recording: `startDate`/`endDate` are UTC instants with a separate `timeZone`, so
every label and day count is computed in the event's zone or a 9am Toronto class
can round onto the wrong day; and multi-day courses are one event spanning first
start to last end, which is what makes `numberOfDays` and the daily window
derivable at all. That holds only because none of our courses use Corsizio's
`breakdownDates` for per-session hours.

**A wrong price was being published to Google.** `structured-data.astro` had a
hardcoded price table listing CSD at 1195 when we charge 995/1095, and it
regex-parsed the free-text frontmatter date, falling back to *today* whenever the
pattern missed, which published permanently-current events. Both are gone: real
ISO dates, and real prices as an `AggregateOffer` when personal and regular
registration differ. Courses with nothing scheduled now emit no Event markup at
all, which is correct, and their "None currently scheduled" button is rendered
from an empty list rather than being a placeholder row someone had to remember to
type.

content.text:
Done. The diff is ready for you to review and commit.

## What's built

**One command, one artefact.** `npm run sync-courses` pulls published Corsizio events and writes `shared/course-schedule.json` (`--dry-run` to preview). Everything downstream reads it.

**Site.** `src/lib/courses.ts` → `workshopsFor(slug)`. Course pages, the "Get Certified" tabs, the workshop buttons and the JSON-LD now all derive from it. Frontmatter keeps `workshops: { heading, body }`; the date array is gone from all seven course files and from the schema, so re-adding one is a build error.

**Email.** `email-automation/courses/*.json` now hold `corsizioEventId` plus only the Zoom/Mural/docs links. `resolveCourseConfig()` does one by-id fetch and fills in date, day count and daily window; a deleted or typo'd event throws rather than falling back to a stale date. `newsletters/courses.json` is deleted — the newsletter builds its Upcoming Courses block from the same generated file.

## Verified, not assumed

- Generated labels come out byte-identical to your hand-written ones (`September 3-4, 2026`, `August 11-14, 2026`).
- `npm run send-course-email --course CSM --dry-run` printed `Corsizio CSM …: Thu, Sep 3, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT – Fri, Sep 4, 2026` and a subject of "Sep 3-4, 2026". Before this change it would have said Jun 15-16, from the stale config.
- Built site: CSPO's dead June entry gone, CSD-nontechnical shows the placeholder and emits zero Event markup, CSM's JSON-LD carries real ISO dates and `AggregateOffer` 795–995 CAD.
- `astro check` 0/0/0, `lint:tw` clean, email-automation `tsc` clean, full build passes.

## Three things worth knowing

**One behaviour change I made deliberately reversible.** CSM's cohort config keeps `"duration": "08:59-17:01"` so its calendar invites are byte-identical to today. Corsizio says 9:00–17:00; the one-minute padding looked intentional, so I preserved it rather than silently changing a student-facing invite. Delete that line to adopt Corsizio's exact times. CSD's hand-typed `12:30-17:00` matched Corsizio exactly, so it's derived now.

**Workshop buttons gained a line.** They now show the daily times (`9:00 AM - 1:00 PM EDT`) under the location. That's what your hand-written "(4 mornings, 9am-1pm ET)" parenthetical was carrying, now derived. Easy to drop from `workshop-buttons.tsx` if you'd rather not have it.

**The sync warns but doesn't fail on an unmapped category.** Add a course category in Corsizio and its events stay invisible on the site until someone adds a row to `CATEGORY_TO_COURSE`. The warning is loud, but it's only visible to whoever runs the sync — if you'd like that to be a hard failure instead, it's a one-line change.

import type { CourseType } from '@/utils/types/types';
import { workshopsFor } from '@/lib/courses';

interface Props {
  course: CourseType;
}

const { course } = Astro.props;

// Every workshop here comes from Corsizio with a real ISO start/end and a real
// price, so there is nothing to parse and nothing to guess. This used to
// regex the free-text frontmatter date and fall back to "today" whenever the
// pattern missed, which published permanently-current events to Google; and
// the price was a hardcoded table that had drifted from what we actually
// charge. Courses with nothing scheduled emit no Event markup at all, which is
// correct: there is no event to describe.
const workshops = workshopsFor(course.id);

/** schema.org wants a plain YYYY-MM-DD for validFrom. */
function isoDate(value: Date): string {
  return value.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

const eventsStructuredData = workshops.map((workshop) => {
  const isVirtual = /virtual|online|self-paced/i.test(workshop.location);

  // A single price is an Offer; a range (personal vs. regular registration) is
  // an AggregateOffer, which is how schema.org expects low/high to be expressed.
  const offers =
    workshop.priceFrom === workshop.priceTo
      ? {
          '@type': 'Offer',
          url: workshop.url,
          availability: 'https://schema.org/InStock',
          price: workshop.priceFrom,
          priceCurrency: workshop.currency,
          validFrom: isoDate(new Date()),
        }
      : {
          '@type': 'AggregateOffer',
          url: workshop.url,
          availability: 'https://schema.org/InStock',
          lowPrice: workshop.priceFrom,
          highPrice: workshop.priceTo,
          priceCurrency: workshop.currency,
          offerCount: 2,
          validFrom: isoDate(new Date()),
        };

  return {
    '@context': 'https://schema.org',
    '@type': 'Event',
    name: `${course.data.name} Training`,
    description: course.data.description,
    startDate: workshop.startDate,
    endDate: workshop.endDate,
    eventStatus: 'https://schema.org/EventScheduled',
    eventAttendanceMode: isVirtual
      ? 'https://schema.org/OnlineEventAttendanceMode'
      : 'https://schema.org/OfflineEventAttendanceMode',
    location: isVirtual
      ? {
          '@type': 'VirtualLocation',
          url: workshop.url,
        }
      : {
          '@type': 'Place',
          name: workshop.location,
          address: {
            '@type': 'PostalAddress',
            addressLocality: workshop.location,
          },
        },
    organizer: {
      '@type': 'Organization',
      name: 'Agile Pain Relief',
      url: Astro.site?.toString() ?? '',
    },
    offers,
    performer: {
      '@type': 'Person',
      name: 'Mark Levison',
    },
    image: new URL(course.data.navigationImage.src, Astro.site).toString(),
  };
});
---

{

content.content:
## Course Config
Create `courses/<type>-<location>.json` (e.g. `csm-virtual.json`, `cspo-virtual.json`, `csd-virtual.json`) with fields:
type, date, numberOfDays, muralLink, meetingInvite (object)

`--course CSM` auto-detects the config by matching files in `courses/` whose name starts with the course type (case-insensitive); it errors if zero or multiple match.

`meetingInvite` is a structured object, both fields copied off the same Zoom screen:
- `zoomUrl` — full Zoom one-click join URL (e.g. `https://us02web.zoom.us/j/...?pwd=...`). Drives the "JOIN the COURSE ZOOM MEETING" button. The `pwd=` token is Zoom's one-click join token.
- `invitationUrl` — Zoom's `/meetings/{id}/invitations?signature=...` link. The email links to it for "all other ways of joining" (phone dial-in numbers, dial-in passcode, SIP). We do **not** scrape or restate those details: Zoom maintains that page, so it stays current automatically when a dial-in number changes. The `signature` token is scoped to the meeting and lives for its lifetime.

The former `passcode` field (plus a hardcoded dial-in number list) is gone. `send-course-email` rejects any config that still has `meetingInvite.passcode`, so an un-migrated config breaks loudly instead of sending a broken invite.

Optional fields (have defaults):
- `duration` — daily start-end time, e.g. `"08:59-17:01"` (default). Drives both the calendar links and the displayed `{{var:class_times}}` in the pre-course emails (e.g. CSD uses `"12:30-17:00"` → "12:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.").
- `timezone` — IANA timezone, e.g. `"America/Toronto"` (default)
- `location` — e.g. `"Virtual"` (default), `"In-Person"`
- `googleDocsFolder` — only needed for CSM courses
- `dropboxFolder` — the **per-cohort mural export** Dropbox folder (post-course only). Shown in the post email as `{{var:training_folder}}`. This is where Mark exports the class's murals after the cohort; it is per-cohort and unrelated to the workbook.
- `workbookUrl` — optional per-cohort override for the hosted workbook link. Normally omitted (the link is resolved by course type; see below). Set it only for a one-off cohort that needs a different URL.

### Post-course workbook link

Two different links live in the post-course email, and they are deliberately separate:

- **Mural export** — `{{var:training_folder}}`, from the per-cohort `config.dropboxFolder`. Changes every cohort. Still on Dropbox (out of scope for the workbook move).
- **Course workbook** — `{{var:workbook_link}}`, the workbook PDF hosted on the APR site. Resolved by `deriveWorkbookUrl(config)` in `src/course-config.ts`: (1) `config.workbookUrl` cohort override, else (2) `courses/workbook-urls.json[type]`, else `null` (course not yet migrated — its template then still hardcodes its own link).

`courses/workbook-urls.json` maps course type → the current direct PDF URL on the APR site (`https://agilepainrelief.com/materials/<course>-<year>-q<quarter>-<hex>/<file>.pdf`). It is the **single place to update once per quarter** when the site's `/materials/` slug rotates. Must be the direct PDF URL (bare files have no folder index) with spaces `%20`-encoded.

`{{var:workbook_link}}` appears in all three CSPO templates — `pre-7day` and `pre-2day` (the "Download the Digital Workbook" link, the pre-class firewall-critical one) and `post` — so migrating a course means switching each of its templates to the variable. (CSM/CSD still hardcode their Dropbox links pending migration.)

---
name: feedback-comments-are-a-smell
description: "Mark almost never writes code/content comments; a needed comment signals the work is badly framed, and every comment already in the repo was AI-generated"

---

Mark almost never writes comments. **Every comment currently in this repo was
AI-generated, not authored by him.** His rule: "if we write a comment it often
suggests the work is poorly written or framed."

**Why:** a comment that explains what code or copy *means* is a patch over
writing that failed to say it. Fixing the naming, the structure or the sentence
removes the need for the note. Comments also rot silently while the thing they
describe moves on.

**How to apply:**

- Default to writing none. Fix the framing instead of annotating it.
- Never cite an existing comment as Mark's intent or preserve one because it
  looks authored. It isn't.

## The TrainerMark Levison is an author, Certified Scrum Trainer®, business consultant, and owner of Agile Pain Relief Consulting. He has introduced Scrum, Lean, and other Agile methods to a broad range of individuals and organizations including Government of Canada departments, major financial and insurance institutions, healthcare agencies, and leading payroll, HR services, and software companies, across Canada and internationally. Mark began his research and practice of Scrum and Agile in 2001, and students now benefit from his more than thirty years of experience in the IT industry and over two decades of Scrum and Agile expertise.

## The CSM Course FormatThe Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) course is an intensive, two-day workshop that introduces and familiarizes you with core Scrum and Scrum methods through direct instruction and hands-on activities.

A distinguishing feature of the training approach: rather than offering a fixed agenda, each workshop is run using Scrum principles to give hands-on experience — using a Product Backlog of topics needed to meet certification requirements plus additional material. Attendees then work as a team with Mark to make choices about what gets added, reordered, and so on.

## Certification & CreditsCourse completion includes a two-year Scrum Alliance professional membership. Each CSM and CSPO course qualifies for 14 PDUs toward maintaining a PMP or other PMI certification, though Agile Pain Relief is a third-party provider not pre-approved by PMI.

## Other Certifications Offered

Beyond the CSM, Agile Pain Relief offers advanced paths:
- **A-CSM** (Advanced Certified ScrumMaster) — long after earning the certification, you retain access to the forum, course materials, and additional resources

Both checks are clean.

## Scrum Alliance vs. what we publish

All five listings on [Mark Levison's SA trainer profile](https://www.scrumalliance.org/trainer-search/trainer/8221) agree with `shared/course-schedule.json`:

| Course | Scrum Alliance | Our site | |
|---|---|---|---|
| CSPO | Tue Aug 11 – 14, 2026, 13:00 UTC | August 11-14, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT | ✓ |
| CSM | Thu Sep 3 – 4, 2026, 13:00 UTC | September 3-4, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT | ✓ |
| CSM | Thu Oct 1 – 2, 2026, 13:00 UTC | October 1-2, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT | ✓ |
| CSPO | Thu Oct 8 – 9, 2026, 13:00 UTC | October 8-9, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT | ✓ |
| CSD | Wed Nov 4 – 6, 2026, 16:30 UTC | November 4-6, 2026, 11:30 AM EST | ✓ |

13:00 UTC is 9:00 AM EDT and 16:30 UTC is 11:30 AM EST, so the times line up too — including the CSD one, which now reads 11:30 AM on both sides. No course on SA is missing from our site, and none of ours is missing from SA.

Two limits on that check: SA publishes no prices, so there's nothing to cross-check against the 795/995 in our JSON-LD; and it shows only a start time, so the daily window (CSPO's 9:00–1:00 four mornings vs. a full day) can't be verified there. Corsizio is the only source for both.

## The four register URLs

Confirmed 4 per class on both pages, all correct:

| # | Where | CSM Sept | CSM Oct |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | JSON-LD `location.url` | `…6bfca0` | `…5f133b` |
| 2 | JSON-LD `offers.url` | `…6bfca0` | `…5f133b` |
| 3 | Register button, Highlights block | `…6bfca0` | `…5f133b` |
| 4 | Register button, Workshops section | `…6bfca0` | `…5f133b` |

Same pattern on CSPO (`…7759ce` for August, `…5f19c5` for October). Each anchor renders next to its own date — September's button links to the September event, October's to October's — and no URL appears against the wrong class.

Worth noting *why* that now holds: all four are fed by the same `workshopsFor(course.id)` call. Before this change, slots 3 and 4 came from the frontmatter array while 1 and 2 came from the regex-parsed date, which is precisely how they could have drifted apart. There's no longer a mechanism for them to disagree.

Sources: [SA trainer profile](https://www.scrumalliance.org/trainer-search/trainer/8221), [SA course search](https://www.scrumalliance.org/courses-events/search)
